title.narrative: Power of Voices Fair For All

description.narrative:
The FAIR For All Project is a five-year project. Its main focus is to support and strengthen Civil Society Organisations to play their diverse roles where value chains are transformed from the dominance of primary commodity exports into a situation where there are better linkages with regional and domestic economies, domestic production and enterprise and the rights of communities, producers and workers are protected and enhanced.
Supporting CSOs today is more crucial than ever as their space to keep duty bearers accountable and providing innovative ways to transform economies. Activists, human rights defenders and journalists are increasingly harassed, and their organizations increasingly face restrictions and struggle to secure sufficient funding.

The Ghana FAIR for ALL Programme has four main focus areas:
1. Strengthen local civil society to collect evidence of rights abuses in primary commodity value chains especially in minerals (gold) and salt value chains, 2. Support communities in seeking redress and hold public and private-sector actors to account. 3. Strengthen civil society to advocate towards mining companies, agribusinesses and their suppliers and traders, primarily through multi-stakeholder engagement, to advance women’s economic empowerment, prevent rights abuses and ensure a living incomes, specifically in Salt and Artisanal gold mining. 4. Promote fiscal and trade regimes that enable better domestic capture of value and transformation in value chains. Ensure value is redistributed to support local value chains that are owned and led by domestic enterprises.
